task.description: Design the fix for ISS-0093: remove (or narrow) the ALTER TABLE ... DISABLE TRIGGER ALL shims in tests/integration/helpers.zig::applyCompatibilityShims() now that GBL-082 has fixed the underlying type mismatch. This is Type E (test-harness code, not CRUD/migration/page/node). Design must specify: (1) which of the six tables' shims can be removed outright vs which (if any) still need a narrower workaround, (2) verification that no other currently-passing integration test implicitly depends on triggers being disabled on these tables (survey callers of TestHarness.init() and any test asserting absence of audit_entries/side effects), (3) exact diff shape for helpers.zig.
acceptance_criteria: Design covers every acceptance criterion in ISS-0093.json's files_to_change
No implementation code present, prose design only
Explicit list of tests at risk of relying on the disabled-trigger behavior, with mitigation for each

result.summary: Designed the ISS-0093 fix: remove the six stale GBL-081 ALTER TABLE ... DISABLE TRIGGER ALL statements (process_definitions, instance_projections, tasks, dead_letter_items, webhook_subscriptions, webhook_deliveries) from tests/integration/helpers.zig::applyCompatibilityShims(), leaving the function and its unrelated legacy-fixture shims (instances table, bpm_test_events_compat_defaults trigger, bpm_repository_artifacts_immutable triggers) intact since they address different problems and are out of scope. Risk survey across all 20 tests/integration/ files referencing audit_entries found 10 currently-failing test cases across 5 files (not just the 3 named in ISS-0093) that this fix repairs with zero test-source changes: TC-ISS-103-INT-02/03/04, TC-OBS-03-INT-01/03, TC-EXT-02-INT-08, TC-OBS-05-INT-02/03, and two unnamed cases in adp06_pipeline_run_correlation_test.zig. No test was found that relies on triggers staying disabled (no test asserts absence of an audit row as desired behavior). webhook_deliveries currently has no trigger of any kind attached in any migration, so its DISABLE statement is presently a no-op; removed anyway for consistency.
